objections.raw_quote: He only offers that one program where it's just one-on-one with him? ... So my question is, maybe it's something that's not necessarily you need. And is it okay with two sessions a week, or is that not enough?
objections.rep_response: Confirmed there is only the one product — "Yes. That's a full transformation in six months working with him" — and answered the frequency question with the standard three to four workouts a week. No smaller, shorter or lighter option was offered or acknowledged to exist, and the rep did not explore why the prospect was asking.

objections.raw_quote: Sounds like a lot to commit to, but I see the point.
objections.rep_response: Did not address it. The prospect immediately moved on to describing his alternatives and the rep followed him rather than isolating the price reaction. No payment structure of any kind was offered at any point on this call.

objections.raw_quote: It's a lot of money and it's a serious commitment. And even if it was $600, I'm not sure I would be able to tell you right now, yes. It's to think about a bit more. But yeah, the financial side is very important as well. If it was $600 for six months. Maybe I could say, yalla, go, let's do it.
objections.rep_response: Ran one diagnostic question first, which was the right instinct — "But is it more about the financial side or the commitment side from you?" — and got "Both." He then made a single price-as-commitment-device argument: "If it was $600, it would be so easy to say, eh, I won't go to the gym today." The prospect rebutted it directly with "$600 is nothing either", and the rep conceded the call immediately: "All right. Cool, man. No worries. If you ever want to reach out, you know where to find us."

objections.raw_quote: I don't think I'm ready to commit for something like this.
objections.rep_response: Followed with the financial-versus-commitment diagnostic and then, after one reframe attempt, accepted the no. None of the OA moves were run — no belief question, no exploration of what was actually preventing him from starting, no return to any goal.

prospect_financials.note: Nothing elicited. The only figures on record are the prospect's own anchor of $600 for six months and his description of his existing semi-private coaching as expensive. No financial-picture question was asked and no payment structure was ever put on the table, despite affordability being named explicitly as half the objection.

evidence: Explicit refusal: "I very much appreciate you taking the time to explain everything to me. I don't think I'm ready to commit for something like this."
Restated and quantified when probed — both money and commitment, with $600 named as roughly the number that would have worked, an order of magnitude below list.
The rep accepted the no within about a minute and booked nothing. No follow-up call, date or action exists.

Counter-evidence for a softer read: the prospect left the door slightly open with "Yeah, I might do that" in response to being told where to find them. That is a courtesy, not a next step, and no mechanism was created to act on it.

Counter-evidence on process rather than outcome: he was never given a payment structure, never asked a commitment question, and never taken through a consequence frame, so this is a no to an offer that was only partially made.
outcome.next_step: None. The rep left an open invitation to reach out and no contact was scheduled.

notable.note: The shortest call in the batch at 21 minutes, and the process largely did not happen. The prospect asked "Tell me about price" twelve minutes in and the rep answered immediately — before any goals depth, any root-cause work, any consequence frame and any commitment check. Two things stand out for a principal. First, the prospect disclosed he was acutely injured that morning — "My back is completely blocked... I played last night and I got hit" — and the rep's only follow-up was a leading closed question, "But there's nothing serious that will disqualify you from working?", before moving on to pitch. Second, no payment structure of any kind was offered here, in a week where the same rep offered an interest-free split to two prospects, a $1,200 monthly plan to a third and third-party financing to a fourth. Affordability was named as half the objection and nothing was put on the table. Separately, this call sits squarely in the documented script gap for a cheaper alternative that worked: he is leaving semi-private coaching he rates highly and choosing between a gym membership and training at home, and none of that was explored.
